evidence: nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/EPT/7-3.3 fetched (Cloudflare-gated to curl; content retrieved via fetcher): 'SECTION 7-3.3 Person paying money to the trustee protected — Estates, Powers & Trusts (EPT) CHAPTER 17-B, ARTICLE 7, PART 3'. § 7-1.5 page verified: 'SECTION 7-1.5 When trust interest inalienable; exception'. § 7-1.19 page verified: 'SECTION 7-1.19 Application for termination of uneconomical trust'. Section text of 7-3.3 (per official page snippets/search-indexed mirror text): 'A person who in good faith transfers money or property to a trustee is not responsible for the proper application of such money or property...'.
notes: VERDICT: neither § 7-1.5 nor § 7-1.19 is the statute safeguarding persons dealing with trustees. § 7-1.5 is the spendthrift/inalienability provision (trust interest inalienable; exception), and § 7-1.19 is an uneconomical-trust termination procedure. The protections for third parties dealing with a trustee live in EPTL Article 7 Part 3 'Rights of Purchasers, Creditors and Other Persons': § 7-3.2 (bona fide purchasers and creditors protected) and § 7-3.3 (person paying money to the trustee protected). For a certification-of-trust/dealing-with-trustee context the correct cite is § 7-3.3 (with § 7-3.2 for good-faith purchasers). Site should replace § 7-1.5 with § 7-3.3.
